full_judgment: 2. The petitioners as plaintiffs instituted the suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in respect of the suit property, a two-storied building with fixture and fittings, situated at Sir Nazimuddin Road within the city of Dhaka. Briefly put, their case before the trial Judge was that the suit property originally belonged to one Hirodehi. One Ajmatul Hoque purchased the same in the name of his wife, Mohsena Khatoon in 1921. In a suit, Title Suit No.10 of 1937, brought by the said Ajmatul Haque against his wife he got his title declared. In the year 1942 he sold out the suit property to one Abdul Hadis Mollah and his two sons, Abdul Rouf Mollah and Abdul Wadud Mollah. Abdul Rouf Mollah died unmarried leaving behind his parents as his heirs. Abdul Hadis Mollah thereafter transferred his share to his wife Khatunnessa by means of a deed of Heba-bil-Ewaj on 3 July 1948. Upon her death Abdul Wadud Mollah got the property as her only heir. He sold out the suit property to the plaintiffs in the year 1982. Their further case was that the previous owner rented out the suit property to the then Muslim Girls' High School, now Anawara Begum Muslim High School for accommodation of girl students. On 8 December 1982 the plaintiffs served a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act on the aforesaid school but the school failed to vacate the suit property.
